summary: Orchestrator handoff conflict leads to split-variant routing during rolling mirror for single-tenant pinned session
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (BrightLens Analytics) observed mixed model outputs for a tenant pinned to gptx-3.7-quant during a rolling mirror prewarm. Traffic that should have remained bound to the pinned variant intermittently routed to the mirror candidate (redwood-rev1) and to a degraded fallback variant. Impact: downstream scoring pipeline received inconsistent embeddings and completions, causing elevated false positives in their analytics dashboard and a temporary billing spike due to requests replayed to fallback variants.

Impact:
- ~4% of requests for tenant T-7243 returned responses from the mirror or fallback variant during 2026-03-10 11:12-11:47 UTC window.
- Customer reported incorrect analytics summaries and asked for credits.

Environment:
- Production tenant on Dedicated capacity in us-east-1.
- Rolling mirror (traffic mirroring to redwood-rev1) was started by BrightLens via Console rollout API.

Observed behavior:
- Explicit tenant version pin present in route metadata, but orchestrator epoch handoff produced two competing route snapshots. Some edge workers evaluated the older snapshot while orchestrator completed commit, creating a transient cohort split. Requests from the same session sometimes hit different model variants and triggered fallback logic.

Expected behavior:
- During rolling mirror/prewarm we expect session affinity + explicit pin to enforce single-variant binding until an explicit promote is completed or pin is removed. No mixing of variants for pinned sessions.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) On dedicated cluster in us-east-1, create a controlled tenant and pin to model gptx-3.7-quant.
2) Start a rolling mirror/prewarm to redwood-rev1 with mirror weight 10% using the Console rollout API and enable prewarm probes.
3) Simulate steady traffic from a tenant session (keepalive stream + intermittent short requests).
4) Trigger orchestrator snapshot replacement (force a config refresh) while prewarm is in progress to reproduce epoch overlap.
5) Observe response model variant ids returned in edge logs and platform trace — verify if any session received mixed variants.
logs: 2026-03-10T11:13:12Z ORCH orchestrator.commit start epoch=513 prev_epoch=512 commit_id=commit-1984
2026-03-10T11:13:15Z SERVING runtime fallback invoked variant=redwood-deg01 reason=prewarm-timeout request_id=rx-7ab
2026-03-10T11:14:05Z PROXY[vpc-ingress] retried upstream due to 502; original request_id=rx-7ac
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: snapshot replacement race between orchestrator and edge snapshot cache TTL caused split-consensus across edge fleet.
Edge cache TTL configured to 2s; orchestrator commit window overlapped prewarm probe bursts leading to some workers loading new snapshot mid-session.
Observed edge logs show consistent epoch flip from 512->513 within ~1s for some workers but not others — indicates non-atomic snapshot activation across region shard boundaries.

Fallbacks triggered when a worker evaluated compatibility checks (model shape/tokenizer) against the new route and fell back to degraded variant. This suggests compatibility policy evaluation was applied atomically with snapshot load, but session affinity check used earlier in-memory token that didn't reconcile.

No evidence of auth or cookie mutation from customer side. Traffic patterns align with orchestrator commit timeline. Related PR that touched snapshot activation order: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/1984 (still under review).
comments: 2026-03-10T12:05Z - Evan Park (assignee): Acknowledged. Reproducing in staging with identical rollout sequence to validate snapshot activation behavior.

2026-03-10T13:22Z - SRE oncall (Marisol Ortega): Found shard-level delay on snapshot propagation to edge pool 3; TTL expiry didn't trigger immediate refresh because cache heartbeat coincided with commit window.
2026-03-10T14:36Z - Aisha Kumar (reporter): Customer confirmed mixed responses for a 30-minute window and provided sample request_ids. Customer requests mitigation and billing credit consideration.

2026-03-11T09:18Z - Eng (Diego Ramos): Confirmed a window where snapshot activation order (compatibility checks then affinity binding) produced transient incoherence. Preparing a patch to reorder activation so affinity binding occurs after snapshot fully materializes.

2026-03-11T16:02Z - Support (Evan Park): Shared temporary mitigation steps with customer: pause mirror weight, drain affected shard, and apply an orchestrator commit with a quiesce window. Customer accepted mitigation and asked for timeline for permanent fix.
resolution: Workaround applied 2026-03-11 16:35Z: paused mirror traffic and performed orchestrator quiesce commit to force atomic snapshot rollout for shard pool 3.

Permanent fix in progress: reorder snapshot activation sequence so that session-affinity binding and explicit pin checks only evaluate after snapshot fully materializes across all regional shards. Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/1992
Customer impact mitigation: issued pro-rated credit for the 35-minute window and created follow-up billing ticket FIN-8842.
Status: monitoring post-workaround for 24h; no further mixed-variant reports from BrightLens.
follow_up_tasks: 1) Deploy orchestrator patch PR#1992 to staging -> canary -> prod (owner: Diego Ramos).
2) Add deterministic quiesce window option to Console rollout API (owner: product infra).
3) Update runbook to include shard-level snapshot propagation checks and a prewarm quiesce recommendation (owner: SRE).
4) Verify telemetry for session-affinity mismatches and add alert rule if >0.1% of pinned sessions see mixed variants for >5m.
